title: Scaffold-grouped inner OOF for the stack
spec: In fit_predict, replace the random KFold(5, shuffle=True) used to build the out-of-fold matrix `oof` with GroupKFold-style folds keyed on the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule (compute with rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, group by string, and assign whole groups to folds with a seeded shuffle). The outer harness already tests on unseen scaffolds, so the meta-learner should see base-model errors that look like that regime. Keep everything else unchanged: same three base models, same LinearRegression(positive=True) meta-learner, same residual baseline.

title: Keep the largest fragment and neutralize charges
spec: Before featurizing, strip salts and small counter-ions by keeping the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser), and neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger. This removes noise from salt forms in SMILES. Apply the same cleanup to train and test molecules. Fall back to the original molecule if sanitization fails.

title: Importance-based feature selection before base models
spec: Inside fit_predict, before the 5-fold OOF loop, fit one LightGBM L1 model (same settings as the existing lg member) on all training rows and read its split-gain feature_importances_. Keep only the top 600 columns by gain, always keeping the SMARTS, physchem and Crippen columns. Apply the same column mask to X and Xte before calling base_predict. The SVR still uses the Morgan block, so keep the first N_BITS columns of the Morgan block inside the kept set so the Tanimoto kernel is unchanged. This shrinks the tree fits and should reduce the noise from the 6000-plus sparse features, with the side benefit of making the 600 s budget easier to meet.

title: Boosting from the SVR offset (init_score stacking)
spec: In base_predict, fit the L1 LightGBM member with its init_score set to the out-of-sample Tanimoto-SVR prediction, so the trees model only what the kernel model leaves over. For the training rows, the SVR prediction is taken from the inner fold it belongs to (or from an inner 3-fold SVR fit on the training rows, to avoid leakage); for the test rows, it comes from the SVR fitted on the full training rows. Predict as svr_pred + lgb_residual_pred. Keep the SVR and the RF-style LightGBM members unchanged. This is a hierarchical stack in which the boosted member corrects the kernel model rather than averaging with it.

title: Elastic-net linear member on standardized features
spec: Add a fourth stack member in base_predict: a sklearn ElasticNet (alpha=0.01, l1_ratio=0.3, max_iter=5000) on the standardized combined matrix. Standardise with the training mean and std, computed inside fit_predict on the training fold and applied to the held-out fold, and clip the standardized values to [-5, 5] so rare bits do not explode. Linear models on fingerprints capture additive group contributions that trees approximate poorly, which may add diversity to the stack. Extend the meta-learner input accordingly and keep LinearRegression(positive=True).

title: Inner out-of-fold grid for SVR C and epsilon
spec: Within fit_predict, before the final stack, select the SVR hyperparameters on the training data alone. Using the precomputed Tanimoto kernel matrix for the training set (computed once), run a small grid over C in {1, 5, 20} and epsilon in {0.05, 0.2} with the same 5-fold split as the stack's inner OOF, and keep the pair with the lowest out-of-fold MAE. Then use the chosen C and epsilon in base_predict. The grid reuses one kernel matrix and adds only six cheap SVR fits per outer fit, so runtime barely changes. This is an automatic hyperparameter search on the kernel member, which has been fixed at C=5 so far.

title: Collision-free unfolded Morgan substructure dictionary
spec: Replace the folded 2048-bit Morgan block in featurize with an unfolded count representation. Using rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with radius 2 and the AdditionalOutput info (or the bitInfo dictionary from GetSparseCountFingerprint), build a vocabulary over the training molecules only, keep substructures seen in at least 3 training molecules, and produce a count matrix indexed by that vocabulary. Test molecules map onto the same vocabulary and unseen keys are dropped. Cap the width at about 3000 columns by keeping the most frequent keys. This removes hash collisions while staying within the RF-free LightGBM and SVR pipeline; the SVR kernel can use the same count matrix with the min-max kernel or the existing Tanimoto form on binarised counts.

title: ExtraTrees member replaces the second LightGBM
spec: In base_predict, replace the second LGBMRegressor (rf) with sklearn ExtraTreesRegressor(n_estimators=300, max_features=0.2, min_samples_leaf=2, n_jobs=8, random_state=seed) fit on the same X and y. Keep the L1 LightGBM and the Tanimoto SVR. ExtraTrees uses random split thresholds, so its errors should be less correlated with the boosted members. Predict on Xte in the same column_stack order.

title: Multi-kernel SVR on fingerprint blocks
spec: Replace the single Tanimoto Morgan kernel in the SVR member with a sum of two precomputed kernels: K = 0.5*Tanimoto(Morgan bits) + 0.5*MinMax kernel on the atom-pair count block. The MinMax kernel is sum(min(a,b))/sum(max(a,b)) over the count columns, computed in numpy by broadcasting in chunks to limit memory. Use the same SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1). Build the train and test kernels from the same column slices so that the blocks match.

title: Median of RF tree predictions
spec: Keep the RandomForestRegressor but, instead of averaging its trees, take the median of the per-tree predictions for each test molecule (np.median over estimators_ predictions, stacked). The median is robust to outlying trees and aligns with an MAE target. Compute per-tree predictions with a loop over model.estimators_.

title: Heavily regularised L1 LightGBM member
spec: In base_predict, add path_smooth=10, lambda_l2=5.0, min_gain_to_split=0.01 and feature_fraction_bynode=0.5 to the objective='l1' LGBMRegressor. Keep colsample_bytree=0.3 and the number of rounds unchanged. Path smoothing shrinks leaf values toward the parent node, which reduces overfitting of leaves on a few noisy logD labels. Leave the other two members as they are.

title: EState and Gasteiger charge block
spec: Add a featurizer block from rdkit.Chem.EState.Fingerprinter.FingerprintMol (the 79-value EState fingerprint: sums of counts and sums of EState indices), and per molecule the mean, minimum and maximum of Gasteiger partial charges computed with rdPartialCharges.ComputeGasteigerCharges, with NaN values set to 0. Append these about 82 columns to X and Xte after the existing descriptor block. The EState fingerprint covers atom-type information that Morgan bits only partly encode. Cache the block per SMILES as desc_matrix does.

title: Kernel PCA embedding of the Tanimoto kernel as extra features
spec: Inside fit_predict, compute the Tanimoto kernel matrix K over the training molecules (the existing tanimoto function on the Morgan bits). Centre K, take its top 10 eigenvectors (np.linalg.eigh, scaled by sqrt of the eigenvalue), and use these as 10 extra features. For test molecules compute the kernel against the training set, centre it with the training means, and project onto the same eigenvectors. Append these 10 columns to the feature matrix before the base models. The projections give the tree models a smooth similarity-space coordinate that bit-level splits cannot express. The projection must use only training-fold molecules, so it is recomputed inside each inner fold to avoid leakage.

title: Bootstrap fraction and more trees
spec: Keep the RandomForestRegressor but set bootstrap=True with max_samples=0.7 (subsampling without replacement-like behaviour) and raise N_TREES to 600. Subsampling adds diversity between trees and lowers the variance of the average. Watch the runtime, which should stay well under the 10-minute limit for 15 fits.

title: Huber-IRLS kernel ridge on the Tanimoto kernel
spec: Replace the SVR member with an iteratively reweighted kernel ridge regression on the precomputed Tanimoto kernel K. Start with weights w=1. At each of about 10 iterations, solve (K + lambda*diag(1/w)) alpha = y with lambda=1.0 via numpy.linalg.solve, compute residuals r = y - K alpha, and set w_i = min(1, delta/|r_i|) with delta=0.3 (Huber weights). This gives a robust, MAE-like kernel regressor. Predict test rows with K_test @ alpha, where K_test is built the same way as in the SVR member.

title: Two-pass hard-example reweighting of the L1 member
spec: Inside base_predict for the first LightGBM member only, run the fit twice. In the first pass, fit the normal L1 model and compute absolute residuals on the training rows, using those from the stack's inner OOF predictions where available. Assign each training row a weight w = clip(1 / (0.1 + |residual| / median|residual|), 0.5, 2.0), so large-error molecules are downweighted as likely label noise and small-error molecules are emphasised. In the second pass, refit the same model with sample_weight=w and the same settings. Keep the second LightGBM member and the stack unchanged. This is a boosting-like reweighting that is cheap because it only doubles one member's cost.

title: Fair-loss objective for the second LightGBM member
spec: In base_predict, the second LightGBM member (the one called rf) still uses the default L2 objective. Change it to objective='fair' with fair_c=1.0, keeping all other settings unchanged. The change is one keyword argument. The L1 objective already gave the largest single gain, so a robust but smooth loss for this member may add diversity to the stack. Leave the first L1 member and the stacking structure as they are.

title: 3D shape descriptors from ETKDG conformers
spec: For each molecule, embed one conformer with rdkit ETKDG using a fixed randomSeed=seed-independent constant (e.g. 42), and if embedding fails fall back to zeros. From the conformer compute the principal moments of inertia (PMI1, PMI2, PMI3), the normalized NPR1 and NPR2, radius of gyration, asphericity, spherocity index and PBF. Cache the results per SMILES in a dict as desc_matrix does, clip to the training 1st/99th percentiles, and append these roughly 8 values to the feature matrix for the base models. No MMFF optimization, so the job stays fast.

title: Crippen atom-type contribution counts
spec: Add the Wildman-Crippen atom-type counts as features. Use rdkit.Chem.rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs (or the per-atom contributions from Crippen) to get the atom type label for each heavy atom, then count how many atoms of each Crippen type a molecule has, across all types seen in the training fold (about 70 to 80 columns). Also append the per-molecule sums of the Crippen MolMR contributions. Keep the existing logP residual baseline as is. This is a fast, interpretable block that a gradient-boosted tree can split on directly.

title: Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprint block
spec: Append an RDKit Gobbi 2D pharmacophore signature to the features. Use rdkit.Chem.Pharm2D.Gobbi_Pharm2D.factory with GetSigFingerprint, then fold the sparse signature to 1024 count bins with a modulo hash so the dimension is fixed. Compute it inside featurize for both train and test, using the training-fold data only for any fitting. Keep the L1 LightGBM and the rest of the stack unchanged; this changes only the input matrix. Cache per SMILES if the timing exceeds about 60 s for 15 fits.

title: Feature-block bagged LightGBM ensemble
spec: Replace the single L1 LightGBM member with three LightGBM models of the same settings, each trained on a random 60% subset of the feature columns drawn from the seed (rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)). Average their predictions as the member output. Each model sees a different slice of the Morgan, atom-pair, torsion, SMARTS and descriptor blocks, which decorrelates the members without adding a new model family. Keep the same number of rounds and learning rate per model, and keep the stack structure unchanged.

title: Scheduled regularisation of the L1 LightGBM member
spec: Vary the regularisation over boosting rounds instead of keeping it fixed. Use LightGBM's reset_parameter callback in the L1 member so that min_child_samples rises linearly from 5 at round 0 to 40 at the final round, and lambda_l2 rises from 0 to 5 over the same schedule. Keep the learning rate at 0.05 and n_estimators at the current value. The idea is to fit fine structure early and then restrict later trees to broader, smoother splits, which may suit the scaffold-held-out test folds. Do not add early stopping or an inner validation split.

title: Small numpy message-passing network as a stack member
spec: Add a fourth base model that is a tiny graph neural network written in numpy. Each atom starts with a feature vector: element one-hot (top 12 elements), degree, formal charge, aromaticity, hydrogen count, and ring membership. Run 3 rounds of message passing where each atom sums neighbour states through a shared linear map followed by ReLU, then sum-pool the atoms into a 64-dimensional molecular vector. Train with Adam (lr 0.005, weight decay 1e-4), L1 loss on the centred residual, 150 full-batch epochs, and a seed-controlled initialisation. Predict the test set from the final weights. Keep the hidden width at 64 so each fit takes only a few seconds on 3000 molecules, and use the output as one column for the meta-learner.

title: FragmentCatalog functional-group hierarchy counts
spec: Add a block of counts from RDKit's FragmentCatalog built from the bundled functional-group parameters (FragmentCatalogParams with the FunctionalGroups catalog). For each molecule, count how many catalog entries match at each level of the hierarchy and store the counts as float columns, dropping entries that match fewer than five training molecules. Build the entry list once from the training fold, then apply the same entries to the test fold so that no test information leaks in. Concatenate the counts after the existing SMARTS block. The goal is coverage of functional groups that the hand-written SMARTS list misses.

title: Drop rare fingerprint bits
spec: Before fitting, remove fingerprint columns (Morgan, atom-pair, topological-torsion, and MACCS if present) that are nonzero in fewer than 3 training molecules, computing the keep-mask from the training fold only and applying it to the test features. This cuts the feature count from about 6,000 to perhaps 2,000 to 3,000 without touching the SMARTS or descriptor blocks. Fewer, better-supported features reduce the random forest's sensitivity to singleton chemotypes and speed up every model, which may also allow more RF trees within the time limit.
